volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Old patches that stored 0…1 linear Volume are converted on load. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

frequency.tooltip: Default slider 0…20 kHz. Pitch MOD can run down through 0. Thru-zero: enable Bipolar on Frequency (domain-add MOD). Domain min/max are slider guides.

morph.tooltip: 0…1 width/duty. 0.5 = center / 50%. Trisaw, Pulse, and Center Square (pulse grows from mid-cycle — not a stepped square). Morph MOD jack on the param row.

amplitude.tooltip: Output level. Slider 0…1 = full-scale bipolar wave. Min/max are guides only — type large values for gain past unity (domain not hard-clamped).

mode.tooltip: Lin = clamp Env to 0…1. Exp = classic VCA CV law (quiet lows, unity at 1) for Amplitude params.

rate.tooltip: Clock rate in Hz. Wired ƒ cancels Rate (absolute Hz), same as oscillators.

duty.tooltip: Gate high time as a fraction of the period. Quantized to whole samples at the current rate.

mode.tooltip: Lin = clamp Env to 0…1. Exp = classic VCA CV law (quiet lows, unity at 1) for Amplitude params.

upShape.tooltip: Rising glide curve. Lin = constant rate. Log = fast start, eases in. Exp = slow start, finishes quickly. Smooth = slow start and end.

downShape.tooltip: Falling glide curve. Lin = constant rate. Log = fast start, eases in. Exp = slow start, finishes quickly. Smooth = slow start and end.

upTime.tooltip: Seconds to reach a higher target from the current value (any amplitude — Hz, CV, audio). 0 = instant.

downTime.tooltip: Seconds to reach a lower target from the current value (any amplitude). 0 = instant.

bias.tooltip: Offset added before slew (0…1). Hidden by default — show it to step the target by hand.

inLow.tooltip: Input value that maps to Out Low. Default 0 (knob/envelope). Use −1 for bipolar audio.

inHigh.tooltip: Input value that maps to Out High. Default 1.

outLow.tooltip: Output at In Low. Default 0 (unit CV / Morph-safe). Pair with Out High for Hz maps.

outHigh.tooltip: Output at In High. Default 1 (unit CV / Morph). Use 1000+ for frequency.

updateOnTrigger.tooltip: On: Attack/Release/curves/Amplitude latch on Gate rise. Off: params apply live.

inputMode.tooltip: Gate = follow high/low (hold at peak while gated). Trigger = rising edge fires one Attack→Release.

attackShape.tooltip: Bipolar segment shape. 0 = linear, + = exponential (fast→slow), − = logarithmic (slow→fast).

release.tooltip: Fall time from current level → 0. 0 = instant snap.

releaseShape.tooltip: Bipolar shape for release. 0 = linear, + = exp, − = log.

order.tooltip: Linkwitz-Riley order: 2 / 4 / 8 (about 12 / 24 / 48 dB/oct). LR4 is the usual default. LR8 is heavier CPU.

frequency.tooltip: Crossover split frequency. When ƒ is wired, that Hz is the split. Unwired uses this knob. Splits stay non-decreasing.

gainDb.tooltip: Input gain into the clipper. Raise this to drive the signal into the tanh curve.

oversample.tooltip: x0 = original tanh. x1 = first-order ADAA (the audible step). x2 = extra linear 2× around the same ADAA — usually inaudible vs x1.

amplitude.tooltip: Scale and invert. 0 = mute, +1 = unity, −1 = invert. Bipolar rational is finer around 0.

mode.tooltip: Real-pole stacks. LP / HP use LPF / HPF. BP is HP then LP. ƒ sets the active cutoff (BP moves both).

slope.tooltip: Cascaded real 1-poles. 6 dB = one pole; 24 dB = four. No resonance.

stagger.tooltip: Pole spread ratio k. 1 = same freq; ~1.5 gentle spread; above ~2.2 a stair-step. No effect at 6 dB.

lowFrequency.tooltip: Highpass cutoff (HP and BP). Sweep / ƒ / 0.1V move cuts together. When ƒ is wired in HP, that Hz is the cutoff.

highFrequency.tooltip: Lowpass cutoff (LP and BP). Sweep / ƒ / 0.1V move cuts together. When ƒ is wired in LP, that Hz is the cutoff.

sweep.tooltip: Shift used cutoffs in semitones. BP keeps the HPF/LPF interval (ratio) constant.

gainCompensation.tooltip: On = scale poles so the labeled cutoff is −3 dB. Off = every pole sits on the staggered freqs. No effect at 6 dB.

oversample.tooltip: Soft Clipper modes on the last stage (the Min→Max knee). x0 original, x1 ADAA, x2 extra linear 2× (usually inaudible vs x1).

gainDb.tooltip: Input drive before the knee. Soft Clipper is the last stage — this is not make-up gain after clip.

minDb.tooltip: Level where the Soft Clipper starts. Below this the driven signal is unchanged.

maxDb.tooltip: Ceiling the tanh curve approaches. A wider Min→Max span makes a more gradual clip.
